title: Read Daniel's own pixel edits to the crow sprite sheet and say what they mean for the look
tier_reason: reading his edit and writing down what it implies — nothing to walk back
ask: Daniel hand-edited Crow in the sprite editor. He left no note, which usually means routine cleanup rather than a decision about the look. The measurement: Crow: 7 pixels across 2 frames (flying 1 · eating a crop, flying 2). The change shows up in: flying, eating a crop. Colors dropped: #f8f4e6. The silhouette moved, not just the interior shading. Look at it against the style guide draft and the rest of the sheet, and say in a few lines what his edit is telling you about the direction — whether it agrees with the guide, quietly contradicts it, or repeats something he has done before. If it is just tidying and there is nothing to learn, say exactly that in one line; a short honest answer beats manufactured significance. Do not propose amendments to the guide yet; he wants a look session before it is signed. This is evidence-gathering for that session.
first_action: Open assets/sprites/generated/crow.png and the ledger entry (step 1) in HQ, compare it with the style guide in docs/design/09-art-direction.md, and write down what the edit says about his taste.

result:
I compared the crow ledger's step 1 with its before and after PNGs and the shipped sheet. Seven opaque #f8f4e6 pixels became transparent: one at frame 1 local (8,14), and six at frame 2 local (4–6,14) and (1–3,15). They sat just below the flying crow's lower edge; no bird color was added or recolored. The current crow.png matches the edited ledger PNG and has no opaque #f8f4e6 left.

This is routine removal of baked cream backdrop, like Daniel's earlier hand cleanup on other sprites. It is consistent with the draft guide's measured hard-alpha edges and does not contradict its palette guidance. These seven pixels offer no new general style preference to decide at the look session. I have not changed the sprite or the unsigned guide.

recommend.question: Hold the look session on the three hand edits we have, or keep collecting first?
recommend.why: All three edits moved the silhouette the same way, so more sheets are likely to repeat the signal rather than add to it.
recommend.instead: Wait for Yuki's next generation batch to be hand-edited too, so the session sees a fresh sheet alongside the three older ones.
